text_blocks.snippet: Air pollution is the contamination of indoor or outdoor air by harmful gases, dust, smoke, or chemical particles that alter the natural composition of the atmosphere.
snippet_highlighted_words: the contamination of indoor or outdoor air by harmful gases, dust, smoke, or chemical particles that alter the natural composition of the atmosphere

list.snippet: Burning Fossil Fuels: Power plants, factories, and residential heating release massive amounts of sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, and greenhouse gases.
Transportation: Vehicle exhausts from cars, trucks, and buses emit nitrogen oxides and particulate matter that drive urban smog.
Industrial Activities: Manufacturing, chemical production, and mining discharge toxic pollutants and volatile organic compounds (VOCs).
Natural Events: Wildfires, volcanic eruptions, and windstorms add large quantities of ash, smoke, and natural dust to the air.
Agricultural Practices: Livestock operations, fertilizers, and pesticide applications emit ammonia and other airborne chemicals.
Primary Pollutants: Substances emitted directly from a source, such as soot from a chimney or exhaust fumes from a car.
Secondary Pollutants: Harmful compounds formed when primary pollutants react in the atmosphere, such as ground-level ozone and photochemical smog.
Particulate Matter (PM2.5 and PM10): Tiny liquid droplets or solid particles fine enough to penetrate deep into the lungs.

Human Health: According to the World Health Organization, breathing polluted air causes respiratory infections, heart disease, strokes, and lung cancer, contributing to millions of premature deaths globally each year.
Ecosystems: Acid rain—created when sulfur and nitrogen oxides mix with atmospheric moisture—damages forests, soils, and aquatic life.
Climate Change: Many air pollutants, particularly carbon dioxide and methane, trap heat in the atmosphere and accelerate global warming.
Transition to Clean Energy: Replacing coal and oil with renewable energy sources like wind, solar, and electric transit significantly lowers emissions.
Regulatory Frameworks: Laws like the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency clean air regulations set legal limits on industrial and vehicular emissions.
Individual Actions: Walking, cycling, using public transit, and improving indoor ventilation help reduce personal exposure and community footprint.

perspectives.title: Kuala Lumpur has topped IQAir’s live ranking of the world’s most polluted major cities, recording an AQI of 211 at 8am on 7 October. The reading puts KL in the “Very Unhealthy” category, as haze continues to blanket the capital. At this level, air pollution can pose health risks to the general population, not just those who are more sensitive to poor air quality. Other Southeast Asian cities also ranked high on the list, including Jakarta, Singapore, Ho Chi Minh City, Hanoi, and Kuching. The worsening air quality comes as parts of the region continue to experience haze, with transboundary pollution also being reported in Malaysia. #SAYSnews
